title: Multiscale entropy (a new standalone op) reproduces NeuroKit2 per scale bit-for-bit -- and the EEG's multi-scale structure

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S002, run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples)
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: Sample entropy measures regularity at one time scale; multiscale entropy (Costa 2002) extends it across coarse-grained scales, separating a structured signal (MSE high or rising at coarse scales) from white noise (MSE falling monotonically). The ecosystem had MSE only inside eegComplexity. This case introduces a standalone op, multiscaleEntropy, completing the entropy family. On a real eyes-closed posterior EEG channel it reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_multiscale (MSEn) BIT-FOR-BIT across scales 1-8 (max |diff| ~4e-16). The finding: the MSE curve is non-monotonic, rising from scale 1 (1.327) to a peak at scale 5 (1.879) and exceeding the scale-1 value, whereas a white-noise series of the same length and SD falls monotonically -- the signature of genuine multi-scale structure in the EEG.

claims.statement: multiscale entropy at scale 1 (= single-scale sample entropy)
multiscale entropy at scale 5 (the peak of the curve)
multiscale entropy at scale 8 (coarsest scale here)
mean MSE across scales 1-8 (the complexity index)
the scale at which MSE peaks
coarse-scale MSE exceeds scale 1 (structure, not white noise)
samples in the analyzed channel (10 s at 160 Hz)

validation.reference: The new standalone multiscaleEntropy op is validated against NeuroKit2 entropy_multiscale (MSEn) on the identical signal, per scale. Both compute the sample entropy (m=2, tolerance r=0.2*SD fixed on the original) of the coarse-grained signal (non-overlapping-window means) at scales 1-8; the per-scale curves agree BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~4e-16). A white-noise series (same N, matched SD) is computed for the structure contrast.
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), subject S002 run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz, 10 s at 160 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the new multiscaleEntropy op reproduces NeuroKit2's per-scale curve bit-for-bit; (2) the MSE curve reveals multi-scale structure. HONEST scope: (1) this is a NEW STANDALONE OP that completes the entropy family in PhysioEEG (sample/approximate/permutation/SVD/dispersion/increment/slope entropies + Lempel-Ziv); multiscale entropy previously existed only inside eegComplexity; (2) it reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_multiscale (MSEn) BIT-FOR-BIT across scales 1-8 (max |diff| ~4e-16) -- the identical coarse-graining (non-overlapping means) and fixed-tolerance sample entropy, so the per-scale curve is a genuine machine-precision match, NOT A CONVENTION AGREEMENT; (3) the finding: the MSE curve is NON-MONOTONIC -- it rises from scale 1 (1.327) to a peak at scale 5 (1.879, ~31 ms at 160 Hz) and the coarse-scale MSE exceeds the scale-1 value; a white-noise series of the same length and SD instead falls MONOTONICALLY (2.16 at scale 1 to 1.08 at scale 8), so the rise is the signature of genuine multi-scale STRUCTURE in the eyes-closed EEG (fast activity plus slower alpha-band dynamics), cross-consistent with the SVD-entropy (low-dimensional) and sample-entropy cases on the SAME data; (4) CAVEAT: at coarse scales the coarse-grained series is SHORT (scale 8 leaves 200 points), so high-scale sample entropy is LESS STABLE -- MSE beyond scale ~10 would need a longer segment; (5) the values are signal properties on one subject/segment; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: The complexity index (area/mean under the MSE curve) and the peak scale are compact single-number summaries useful for group comparison; both depend on the maximum scale and the segment length. On a longer recording, extending to scales 1-20 and comparing conditions (eyes-open vs eyes-closed, or across the scalp) would test whether the coarse-scale rise tracks the alpha rhythm. Documented, not escalated.
